newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Ten firms compete to advise on Brazil's CPFL sale.
newsitem.headline: Ten firms compete to advise on Brazil's CPFL sale.

text.p: Sao Paulo state government said it received 10 proposals on Wednesday from consultants interested in advising on the sale of power distributor Companhia Paulista de Forca e Luz (CPFL), expected for August.
The state government will receive on Thursday and Friday proposals from firms competing for contracts to advise on the sale of power firms Eletropaulo and Cesp, respectively.

Three groups are bidding for contracts for the so-called A service to make a financial evaluation of the firm, said Ricardo Lima, an official at the Sao Paulo state Energy Secretariat who advises investors on the state's privatization plan.
The other seven groups are bidding for contracts for B service, which includes financial evaluation, equity restructuring and designing a privatization model for the company, he added.
Lima said the winning groups are expected to be announced by late February or early March noting that consultants will have 120 days to complete the evaluations.
The following groups are competing for the A service:
* Group 1 - Grupo Trevisan, Arthur D. Little, BSB Engenharia and Banco Liberal;
* Group 3 - Banco Fator, Fator projeto, Azevedo Sodne, Ernst & Young, Themag and Paribas.
He also listed the groups competing for the B contract as follows:
* Group 1 - Banco Fator, Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, Azevedo Sodne, Ernest Young, Themag and Paribas.
* Group 2 - Graphus, Kleinwort Benson, CS First Boston, Unibanco and Engevix.
* Group 3 - Maxima, SBC Warburg, Morgan Stanley and Omega.
* Group 4 - Salomon Brothers, Banco Patrimonio and Schroder.
* Group 5 - J.P. Morgan, Goldman Sachs, Garantia and BVI.
* Group 6 - Bozano, Simonsen, BZW, Leman Brothers, Stone & Webster and Wald Associados.
* Group 7 - Projeto, Merrill Lynch, Rotchschild and ABN-Amro bank.
